newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: At least three injured in Kosovo explosions.
newsitem.headline: At least three injured in Kosovo explosions.

text.p: At least three people were injured on Wednesday when an explosive device went off in Pristina, the capital of the volatile Serbian province of Kosovo, police sources said.

Witnesses said the explosive device was placed in a garbage container in front of the Faculty of Philosophy beside the monument of Vuk Karadzic, the Serbian language reformer, in the centre of the city.
One senior Serbian official told Reuters another explosive device, also placed in a garbage container, went off at the same time in Prizren beside the monument of Serbian King Dusan.
This could not immediately be confirmed and there were no reports of any casualties or damage in the town south of Pristina.
Police sources believe the explosive devices were planted by a group which has been carrying out terrorist attacks in Kosovo over the past year.
The latest attacks follow several weeks of quiet in the mostly Albanian populated province after Serbian police arrested some 70 people in a widely-publicised "anti-terrorist" sweep in January.

The clandestine Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) is reported to have been behind several guerrilla attacks over the past year in which more than 30 people, including ethnic Albanians loyal to Belgrade and Serbians, have died.
One young ethnic Albanian died in prison under torture after the crackdown, western officials said.
Serbian police shot dead three Albanians in a gunbattle during the operation, killing a suspected commander of the outlawed KLA.

In 1989 Serbia's autocratic President Slobodan Milosevic removed Kosovo's autonomous status, accusing the Albanian majority of preparing to secede. Albanians outnumber Serbs by nine to one in the province.
The province has since been widely regarded as a powder keg that could destroy international peace efforts in the Balkans.
The latest violence coincides with preparations for talks on the status of Albanians in Kosovo due to be held between Serbian officials and an ethnic Albanian leader in New York in April.
